missions.doToday: Write down 10 skills and star 3.
missions.mission: Open a blank doc and list 10 things people already ask you for help with — spreadsheets, cooking, resumes, car repairs, photo edits, anything. Star the three you could do for money without learning anything new. This list is your raw material; every day after today works off it.
missions.replyPrompt: What's your #1 starred skill — and why is it obvious to you that people would pay for it?
missions.title: Inventory every skill you have

missions.doToday: Write your one-lane sentence and reply it to this email.
missions.mission: Choose ONE skill from yesterday's starred three — the one you'd do for free because it's fun, and that someone paid for at least once (even a friend's coffee counts). Write it down as a sentence: "I help [who] with [skill]." Cross the other two out for the next 28 days. One lane beats three half-lanes.
missions.replyPrompt: What's your lane sentence? Hit reply with it — I'll hold you to it.
missions.title: Pick one lane, kill the rest

missions.doToday: Write your buyer profile: who, what problem, where they hang out.
missions.mission: Get specific about who pays. Write down: one type of person (e.g. "new landlords," "busy moms," "restaurants"), what they're struggling with that your skill fixes, and where they hang out online or offline (a Facebook group, a neighborhood, a coworking space). If you can't name where they are, you can't reach them — keep narrowing until you can.
missions.replyPrompt: Where do your buyers actually hang out? Name the group, street, or platform.
missions.title: Name the buyer, not the crowd

missions.doToday: Draft your one-paragraph offer in a doc.
missions.mission: One paragraph, three parts: who it's for, what changes for them, what it costs. Example: "I do kitchen declutter plans for busy parents — you get a room-by-room plan in 48 hours, $80." No websites, no logos. Draft it in a doc, then read it out loud — if a stranger wouldn't understand it, rewrite it until they would.
missions.replyPrompt: Paste your draft offer — I'll tell you the first thing a buyer would ask.
missions.title: Write your first offer

missions.doToday: Write down your price + one-sentence reason.
missions.mission: Price your first version low enough to get yeses fast, high enough to feel real. Rule of thumb: enough that 5 sales cover one solid day's wages for you. Write down your price and your reason in one sentence — "I'm charging $X because [reason]." You will raise it later; today's price is a door-opener, not a forever number.
missions.replyPrompt: What did you price it at, and what's the reason?
missions.title: Set your first price

missions.doToday: Build your one-page proof sheet and export it as PDF.
missions.mission: Buyers don't trust claims, they trust evidence. Make a one-page doc (Google Docs is fine) with: your offer paragraph, 2-3 examples of past work (photos, screenshots, even practice pieces), and one line about who you are. This is your "proof sheet" — you'll send it instead of pitching into the void.
missions.replyPrompt: What's the strongest piece of proof on your sheet?
missions.title: Build a one-page proof sheet

missions.doToday: Send 3 personal messages (text, DM, or email — not a group blast).
missions.mission: Message 3 people you already know — friends, ex-coworkers, family — with a personal note, not a blast. "Hey, I'm starting to offer [offer] — $X. Know anyone who might need this?" Warm asks convert 10x better than cold posts. Their job isn't to buy; it's to react and refer.
missions.replyPrompt: Who did you message, and what did the first reply say?
missions.title: Send it to 3 warm people

missions.doToday: Ask 10 people, record their exact words in your doc.
missions.mission: Find 10 people in your buyer lane (from Day 3's "where they hang out") and ask one question: "Quick question — is [their problem] something you're dealing with right now?" Reddit threads, Facebook groups, comments sections, local shops. You're collecting language, not selling — write down the exact words they use to describe the problem.
missions.replyPrompt: What phrase did you hear more than once? Quote it.
missions.title: Ask 10 strangers one question

missions.doToday: Rewrite your offer paragraph in their words; update your proof sheet.
missions.mission: Take yesterday's notes and rewrite your offer using the exact phrases buyers used. If they said "my inbox is a nightmare," your offer says "tame your nightmare inbox" — not "email productivity optimization." Speak their language and the offer starts selling itself.
missions.replyPrompt: What's one word buyers use that you never would have picked?
missions.title: Rebuild your offer in their words

missions.doToday: Message one person with the free-with-a-review offer.
missions.mission: Pick ONE person from Day 8 who had the problem and offer the full thing free — with one condition: they give you an honest review and let you share before/after proof. Free work with a receipt (testimonial + proof photos) is worth more than ten silent paid gigs. Set a deadline so it doesn't drag.
missions.replyPrompt: Who did you pick, and what's the deadline you set?
missions.title: Deliver one free (strategically)

missions.doToday: Deliver the work; save before/afters, time spent, and all messages.
missions.mission: Deliver yesterday's free job like a paying client is watching — because future ones are. Take before/after photos or screenshots at every step, note how long each step takes, and save every message. This documentation becomes your process, your pricing data, and your proof.
missions.replyPrompt: How long did it actually take? Was it more or less than you guessed?
missions.title: Do the work, document everything

missions.doToday: Publish one proof post in one place.
missions.mission: Write one short post for wherever your buyers hang out (Day 3): the problem (their words), what you did, the before/after, and a soft call to action — "Doing 3 more of these this week, $X." Attach the before/after photo. One post, one place, no hashtags soup. Proof + scarcity beats a sales pitch every time.
missions.replyPrompt: Link it or screenshot it — where did you post, and what's the first reaction?
missions.title: Turn proof into a post

missions.doToday: Send 5 follow-up messages.
missions.mission: Message everyone who liked, commented, or DMed about your post — plus the 3 warm people from Day 7 you haven't heard back from. One line: "Hey, still have 2 spots this week for [offer] at $X — want one?" Most sales die from no follow-up, not from rejection. Send 5 follow-ups today.
missions.replyPrompt: How many of the 5 replied? What did the yes/no split look like?
missions.title: Follow up like a professional

missions.doToday: Get one paid yes and take payment.
missions.mission: Today is about getting the first paid yes. If someone's warm, ask directly: "Want me to start yours today? I can take payment by [Venmo/Zelle/Cash App/Stripe link]." If nobody's warm, repost yesterday's proof post in a second place and send 5 fresh outreach messages. The goal is ONE paid booking — even discounted — with money in your account by tonight.
missions.replyPrompt: Did you close one? If yes — what finally tipped them? If no — what's the blocker?
missions.title: Close customer #1

missions.doToday: Create your payment link + booking form + canned reply.
missions.mission: Kill the DM chaos. Set up three things: a payment link (Stripe Payment Links, Venmo business, or Cash App — pick one), a booking form (Google Forms with 5 fields: name, contact, what they want, deadline, how they found you), and a canned reply you paste to every inquiry with the price + the form link. Paste-to-book beats back-and-forth every time.
missions.replyPrompt: Which payment tool did you pick, and why?
missions.title: Build your simple booking flow

missions.doToday: Update your price everywhere: proof sheet, posts, canned reply.
missions.mission: You have proof, a process, and at least one paid customer. Raise your price 20% today and update the proof sheet. If your price was $80, it's $96 now (round it: $95 or $100). Buyers anchor on your confidence — and the customers you lose at the new price were never going to sustain you anyway.
missions.replyPrompt: What was your old price vs. your new one — and how did it feel to change it?
missions.title: Raise the price 20%

missions.doToday: Write your numbered delivery checklist (steps + time each).
missions.mission: Turn your Day 11 notes into a numbered delivery checklist — every step in order, with time estimates. Next time you get a booking, you work the list instead of improvising. Checklists cut delivery time, kill forgotten steps, and let you train someone else later. Save it as a reusable template.
missions.replyPrompt: How many steps is your checklist — and which step eats the most time?
missions.title: Systemize delivery with a checklist

missions.doToday: Send the referral ask to all past customers (even the free one).
missions.mission: After each delivery, send this: "Glad you're happy! Quick favor — do you know 2 people who'd want the same? I'll give them your price." Referrals from happy customers close at 3-5x the rate of cold outreach and cost you nothing. Build the ask into your checklist as the final step. Send it to every past customer today.
missions.replyPrompt: How many referrals came back, and who surprised you?
missions.title: Ask every customer for referrals

missions.doToday: Write your three tiers with names, what's included, and prices.
missions.mission: Turn your single offer into three tiers: Basic (what you sell now), Standard (basic + one valuable extra, ~1.6x price), Premium (standard + done-for-you or rush delivery, ~2.5x price). Most buyers pick the middle — and the premium tier exists to make the middle look reasonable. Update your proof sheet with all three.
missions.replyPrompt: What extra did you put in the Standard tier?
missions.title: Package it — good/better/best

missions.doToday: Name your #1 channel and commit to a weekly rep number.
missions.mission: Look at where every customer so far came from: the post, the referral, the warm message, the group. Pick the ONE channel that produced the most and double down on it this week — same place, same format, more reps. One channel done well beats five done halfway. Write down your channel and your weekly rep target (e.g. "2 proof posts per week in the moms group").
missions.replyPrompt: What's your channel, and how many reps per week?
missions.title: Find one repeatable channel

missions.doToday: Build the tracker; fill in every customer to date.
missions.mission: Open a spreadsheet with columns: name, date, channel, tier, price paid, referred by, testimonial received (y/n). Enter every customer so far. Your only goal for the rest of the sprint: 10 rows. What gets measured gets filled — and this sheet becomes your business's memory.
missions.replyPrompt: How many rows do you have right now — and which channel owns the most?
missions.title: Build your 10-customer tracker

missions.doToday: Name your add-on, price it, add it everywhere.
missions.mission: Look at your tracker and messages: what do customers keep asking for on top of the core offer? Turn the most common request into a named add-on with its own price (e.g. "+$40 rush delivery," "+$60 extra room"). Add-ons raise average order value without new customers. Add it to your proof sheet and canned reply today.
missions.replyPrompt: What's the add-on — and is it something you already do for free?
missions.title: Productize the most-requested extra

missions.doToday: Post the flash offer with a hard deadline.
missions.mission: Post this in your #1 channel: "Flash offer — [offer] at [10-15% off], 3 spots, ends in 48 hours." Scarcity + deadline + discount moves fence-sitters. Honor the deadline strictly — when it's over, it's over. The point isn't the discount; it's learning to create urgency on demand.
missions.replyPrompt: How many of the 3 spots filled — and what did buyers say about the deadline?
missions.title: Run a 48-hour flash offer

missions.doToday: Get 3 story-format testimonials with permission to publish.
missions.mission: Go back to every happy customer and ask for a testimonial with this structure: the problem before, what you did, the result after — plus permission to use their first name and photo. Generic "great work!" quotes don't sell; stories do. Aim for 3 solid story-testimonials today, then add the best one to the top of your proof sheet.
missions.replyPrompt: Paste your best one — problem, what you did, result.
missions.title: Collect every testimonial properly

missions.doToday: Raise prices again; update proof sheet, posts, canned reply.
missions.mission: Second price raise of the sprint: another 15-20%, or move your Standard tier to your old Premium price. You've got testimonials, a checklist, tiers, and a channel that works — that's a realer business than Day 1. Update everything. Notice: raising prices on proof is a skill, and you're practicing it.
missions.replyPrompt: New prices — and did anyone push back? What did you say?
missions.title: Raise prices again (and mean it)

missions.doToday: Publish one teaching post or 60-second video.
missions.mission: Share one thing you learned in a post or short video in your channel: a mistake, a shortcut, a before/after with the lesson. Teaching builds authority faster than selling — buyers come to the person who obviously knows the craft. End with a soft line: "I do this for clients too — 2 spots next week."
missions.replyPrompt: What did you teach — and did anyone ask about hiring you from it?
missions.title: Teach it once, publicly

missions.doToday: Write your one-page weekly rhythm.
missions.mission: Design your sustainable week on one page: how many delivery slots, how many outreach reps, one rest day. Example: "Mon/Wed/Fri: 2 delivery slots. Tue/Thu: 1 outreach post + 5 follow-ups. Sat: admin. Sun: off." A side stream survives on rhythm, not motivation. Write yours and put it where you'll see it.
missions.replyPrompt: What's your weekly rhythm — and which day is sacred off?
missions.title: Build your weekly rhythm

missions.doToday: Automate one repetitive task; note the time it saves.
missions.mission: Pick the single most repetitive task in your flow — answering the same questions, sending the same follow-ups, invoicing — and automate it with a free tool: a canned-reply doc, a Calendly link, a Google Form auto-reply, a Zapier free-tier zap. One automation today; the goal is buying back an hour a week, forever.
missions.replyPrompt: What did you automate — and how much time does it save per week?
missions.title: Automate one annoying task

missions.doToday: Fill in the totals; write your 3 proud numbers + 1 leak.
missions.mission: Open your tracker and add it up: total revenue, total hours, revenue per hour, customers, refunds. Write down three numbers you're proud of and one thing that leaked money or time. This is your baseline — every future decision gets measured against it. No judgment, just arithmetic.
missions.replyPrompt: Total revenue and revenue per hour — what are your numbers?
missions.title: Count the money, honestly

missions.doToday: Write the 5-line plan and tell one person.
missions.mission: Write your next-30-day plan in five lines: your lane (unchanged or narrowed?), your price, your channel, your weekly reps, your revenue target. Then message one person — a customer, a friend, anyone — and tell them the plan out loud. Public commitments stick. Day 30 isn't the finish line; it's the first day you run it without the training wheels.
missions.replyPrompt: Paste your 5-line plan — what's the revenue target for the next 30?
missions.title: Commit to the next 30
